re_line: Lai's National Day address, militia boat off Taiwan's east coast, EU caps Chinese hybrids, China's base in Laos, House scrutiny of Hong Kong and Webull
editors_note: This is the second China Room Brief. It arrives every Tuesday with a recap of the past week in U.S.-China relations and a look ahead.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Senators link spy case on Lai's son to CCP surveillance
heard_on_the_hill.body: Republican Senators Blackburn, Ricketts and Scott called the case against Zhang Wanying evidence that the CCP is exporting repressive surveillance to the U.S., VOA Chinese reported. Prosecutors charged Zhang with acting as an unregistered PRC agent after she allegedly surveilled an adult child of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te in Seattle; the FBI arrested her October 4 at Los Angeles International Airport. China's foreign ministry said it was unaware of the case.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Moolenaar seeks review of Hong Kong's Fed facility access
heard_on_the_hill.body: House Select Committee on the CCP Chairman John Moolenaar called for a review of Hong Kong's access to a Federal Reserve liquidity facility, per a committee release. CNBC reported he wants the Fed to reconsider the city's dollar-swap access as China promotes the renminbi as a global reserve currency.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: House China panel faults Webull over China links
heard_on_the_hill.body: Webull Financial "has not been transparent about its links to China," a bipartisan Select Committee investigation led by Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) and Ranking Member Ro Khanna (D-CA) found. The brokerage's shares fell after the panel flagged the ties, Reuters reported.

heard_on_the_hill.headline: Bennet, other lawmakers visit Taiwan after Trump-Xi summit
heard_on_the_hill.body: Several members of Congress are visiting Taiwan after last month's Trump-Xi summit, VOA Chinese reported, with AIT saying the visits reinforce the U.S.-Taiwan partnership. Senator Michael Bennet is in Taiwan this week to meet senior officials on regional security.

in_the_news.headline: Lai says Taiwan will not give up its freedom; Beijing calls him 'pragmatic independence worker'
in_the_news.body: President Lai Ching-te told Double Ten crowds in Taipei that Taiwan "cherishes peace" but will not give up its freedom, the Washington Post reported, and pledged NT$1.1 trillion ($34.5 billion) for defense in 2027. Beijing's Taiwan Affairs Office called him a "pragmatic Taiwan independence worker," while the U.S. welcomed his commitment to Taiwan Strait stability. China then announced live-fire drills across four seas running October 12 to 20.

in_the_news.event: Chinese militia boat off Taiwan's east coast
in_the_news.headline: China militia boat spotted for first time off Taiwan's east coast
in_the_news.body: A Taiwanese patrol spotted a Chinese maritime militia boat off Taiwan's east coast for the first time, Reuters reported October 8. A State Department spokesperson said China's patrols there "only exacerbate tensions." Taiwan officials believe the regular coast guard patrols China has run off the east coast since June are rehearsals for a maritime blockade.

in_the_news.headline: China, EU step back from trade war with limits on hybrid car exports
in_the_news.body: A deal with Beijing could roughly halve hybrid vehicle shipments from China over the next four years, the European Union said, the New York Times reported. Bloomberg put the cap at 350,000 units a year, following talks between Maroš Šefčovič and Commerce Minister Wang Wentao on October 8 and 9. MOFCOM said the deal secures China's "export space" in Europe.

in_the_news.headline: China expands military reach with new base in Laos
in_the_news.body: China is building a military facility with a new runway at Ban Keun, Laos, the New York Times reported. Reuters satellite imagery showed attack aircraft and military vehicles at the site, while an analysis in The Diplomat counted eight Chinese training aircraft and described the facility, opened September 29, as a joint support center rather than an attack base.

in_the_news.headline: China nominates health official to lead WHO
in_the_news.body: Song Li, a senior official of the All-China Women's Federation, is Beijing's nominee for WHO Director-General, Reuters reported. The Washington Post tied the bid to Beijing's push to fill multilateral leadership gaps amid reduced U.S. engagement with UN institutions.

research_roundup.headline: FAQ | ANOTHER CEASEFIRE: CAN THE US AND CHINA END THEIR TRADE WAR?

research_roundup.event: PLA lessons from Ukraine drone war
research_roundup.headline: Learning Without Bleeding: China’s Lessons from the Russia-Ukraine Drone War
research_roundup.body: Lilly Min-Chen Lee and Kateryna Bondar trace how quickly Chinese analysts identify battlefield innovations from the Russia-Ukraine drone war and how the PLA translates those lessons into training, procurement, hardware and force structure.

research_roundup.event: Chinese research vessels near subsea infrastructure
research_roundup.headline: China’s Weaponization of Dual-Use Research Vessels for Undersea Data Dominance
research_roundup.body: Analyzing 223 vessels, Jose M. Macias III, Tao-Hung Chang, Nico Vacca and Benjamin Jensen find that Chinese research ships spend an unusually large share of time near subsea infrastructure on the high seas. They call for stronger allied monitoring, coordinated patrols and faster cable repair.

research_roundup.headline: Russia’s Turn to China Under Sanctions: Sanctions Decay, Substitution Elasticity, and the Challenge of Sustaining Pressure
research_roundup.body: Damien Spleeters argues that sanctions lose force not only when governments stop updating them but also when targeted actors replace restricted products, suppliers and acquisition channels faster than controls can adapt.

research_roundup.headline: Understanding the Chinese-Language Media Landscape in Southeast Asia
research_roundup.body: Lauren Mai, Andreyka Natalegawa, Gregory B. Poling and Japhet Quitzon argue there is no viable strategy for countering Chinese information warfare without buy-in from regional partners and awareness of the scale, scope and impact of Chinese-language media in the region.
